name: Graph Random-Walk Generation
problem_statement: Generate vertex sequences sampled from a declared graph transition process.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

problem_inputs.name: start_vertices
problem_inputs.description: One starting vertex per walk; repeats are permitted.

required_outputs.name: walks
required_outputs.description: One sequence per start; a dead end terminates the walk.

solution_semantics.objective: Sample walks from the specified transition probabilities.
solution_semantics.exactness: Every transition must be valid and obey the requested probability distribution; finite samples are stochastic outputs.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Each walk starts at its requested vertex and follows graph edges.
Distribution tests on small graphs agree with analytic transition probabilities.
Walk lengths do not exceed the requested limit.
edge_cases: A dead-end start yields a one-vertex sequence.
Zero total outgoing weight terminates a weighted walk.

correctness: Each walk starts at its requested vertex and follows graph edges.
Distribution tests on small graphs agree with analytic transition probabilities.
Walk lengths do not exceed the requested limit.
